name: metabolism-biomass-yield-s1-diagnostic
title: Re-measure biomass yield on a recorded commit, and discriminate one defect from two
question: On a fresh basal run whose code revision is recorded, what is the biomass yield - and does carbon close at the same time? The first half removes the provenance ambiguity in the committed fixtures; the second half is the discriminator, because if carbon closes at baseline while yield sits above the first-principles ceiling, the baseline defect is energetic and therefore distinct from the carbon creation seen under a binding uptake cap.

evidence.provenance_limitation: The measured side is the committed tests/fixtures/population_phenotype_basal/ fixtures, which stamp reconstructed: True, commit: None, sweep_dir: None, baked: unknown. The exact code and sweep that produced 0.826 were never recorded, so this value cannot be attributed to any particular revision of the model.

assumptions.text: A single 4-seed x 8-generation run with generation_lower_bound 3 (the 20 post-burn-in cells the committed fixtures record) is a like-for-like re-measurement of the blessed ensemble - same config, same cache, same burn-in window - so a divergence in Yxs is attributable to code or to the unrecorded provenance of the fixtures rather than to a different experimental design.

★ No absolute plausibility band is claimed for the implied biomass carbon content, on purpose. The only in-repo range for it (~0.45-0.50 gC/gDW, scripts/render_basal_vs_ literature.py:77) is an uncited constant, its units may be a slip from biomass YIELD (gDW/g glucose), whose curated band happens to overlap the same numbers, and the repo contradicts itself elsewhere (tests/test_basal_vs_literature.py:122 uses 0.40-0.55). So this study makes no absolute claim and rests only on the relative contrast against the binding-cap condition. Grading the content absolutely needs the model's OWN composition-derived carbon content as the reference - an internal consistency check requiring no literature - which is left to a later study (see the investigation's decisions_needed).

★ The carbon-closure evidence here is NOT the same statistic as the overflow titration's 1.11 / 7.93. Those are closure ratios computed against an independent estimate of biomass carbon. This study instead computes biomass carbon BY DIFFERENCE (glucose_C - CO2_C - 2*acetate_C), which makes the closure ratio 1.0 by construction and moves all the information into the implied carbon CONTENT - 0.4549 gC/gDW here. That number is the real test: if the model were creating carbon at baseline the by-difference content would come out implausible or negative, and it does not. So this is strong positive evidence for two distinct defects, but it is not a like-for-like comparison against the overflow numbers. Making it like-for-like needs the overflow runner's closure estimator, which lives only on the overflow branch and is deliberately out of scope here.

model_settings.name: no-model-change
model_settings.detail: Diagnostic only. This study runs current main unmodified; the fix is a later, separate study with its own parity gate and golden regeneration.

tests.name: biomass-yield-remeasured-on-recorded-commit
tests.question: Does a fresh run on a recorded commit reproduce the committed fixture's Yxs of 0.826 gDW/g glucose, and does it still exceed the 0.538 first-principles ceiling?

measure.detail: Yxs = dDW / integral(q_glc * DW) dt by direct mass balance over post-burn-in cells, via the canonical estimator (physiology_from_sweep / render_basal_vs_literature.py --from-sweep). Graded on the same physiology.biomass_yield axis the basal card uses - literature criterion, measured band 0.355-0.444, theoretical_max 0.538.

tests.name: carbon-closure-discriminates-one-defect-from-two
tests.question: Does carbon close at baseline while yield exceeds the ceiling - the signature of an energetic defect distinct from the binding-cap carbon creation?

measure.detail: Carbon closure = (CO2 + 2*acetate + biomass carbon) / (6 * glucose), plus RQ = CO2/O2, computed from the same sweep parquet via the exchange fluxes in bake_model_metabolism.py. Reference points from the overflow titration: closure 1.11 at a slack cap, 7.93 under a binding cap.

biomass-yield-remeasured-on-recorded-com.detail: Yxs 0.8313 gDW/g glucose (20 cells, CV 1.44%) - 1.87x the top of the measured band 0.355-0.444 and 1.55x the first-principles ceiling 0.538. Reproduces the committed fixture 0.8257 to within 0.67%, which is inside the ensemble CV.

carbon-closure-discriminates-one-defect-.detail: Implied biomass carbon 0.4549 gC/gDW - an unremarkable value giving no sign of carbon creation, so carbon accounting is self-consistent at baseline. See the assumption below on the provenance of the comparison range: it is an uncited in-repo constant, NOT a curated reference. Exchanges (mmol/gDW/h): glucose 4.810, O2 0.463, CO2 1.590, acetate 0.000; O2:glucose 0.096, CO2:glucose 0.331, RQ 3.43 against ~1 for full oxidation. PASS means the discriminator resolved, not that the model is healthy.

findings.statement: On a run whose commit is recorded, the baseline makes 0.831 gDW per gram of glucose - 1.87x the top of the measured band and 1.55x the first-principles ceiling - and the run shows no sign of the gross carbon imbalance that appears under a binding uptake cap. Implied biomass carbon comes out at 0.455 gC/gDW, an ordinary value, against a binding-cap condition where closure degrades to 7.93. The comparison that carries this is RELATIVE: two conditions of the same model behaving qualitatively differently. A single mass-bookkeeping defect would break conservation in both. What the baseline fails to do is respire: O2:glucose is 0.096 and RQ is 3.43 against ~1 for full oxidation, so 94.5% of glucose carbon is retained as biomass and almost none is burned for maintenance and ATP. The violation is therefore energetic in origin - the cell builds biomass it never pays the ATP cost for - and is a different failure from the carbon creation the binding cap triggers. Two defects, not one.

expected.summary: A pure mass-bookkeeping defect should break carbon conservation everywhere it is exercised. The overflow titration shows closure of 1.11 at a slack cap and 7.93 under a binding cap, so if one bug drove both, baseline carbon accounting should also be visibly broken. It is not.

findings.next_action: Scope the fix around the energetic side - maintenance-ATP / NGAM-GAM parameterization and respiratory capacity - rather than around mass bookkeeping. Enzyme-capacity constraints remain downstream of this: they bite when a cell pushes respiration to its ceiling, and this model barely respires.

findings.statement: The fresh run gives Yxs 0.8313 against the committed fixture's 0.8257, a difference of 0.67% - well inside the ensemble CV of 1.44%. Growth rate 0.851 vs 0.814 and glucose uptake 4.81 vs 5.14 are likewise close. So the fixture's headline number is reproducible on current main even though its provenance was never recorded, and the first_principles_violation verdict standing since 2026-06-17 is not an artefact of a stale or unattributable bake.

expected.summary: The committed fixtures stamp reconstructed: True, commit: None, sweep_dir: None, baked: unknown, so agreement was not guaranteed and a material divergence would itself have been the finding.

findings.next_action: No re-bake. The fixtures are the reference everything else is graded against and moving them mid-investigation shifts that reference; this run is evidence for #296 (auto re-bake / re-grade), not a reason to pre-empt it.
